children.name: The AI Enablement Audit
children.blurb: The AI Enablement Audit is a structured review of an organization's readiness to deploy AI systems safely and lawfully.

children.name: Threat Modelling for Legal AI
children.blurb: Threat modelling for legal AI examines how a system that drafts, reviews, or researches legal content can fail in ways that harm clients, privilege, or case outcomes.

children.name: Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation
children.blurb: Data loss prevention and sanitisation in AI security audits covers the controls that stop sensitive or regulated information from entering model training sets, prompts, retrieval contexts, or generated outputs.

children.name: Shadow AI in Legal Teams
children.blurb: Shadow AI in legal teams covers any AI tool or model that lawyers, paralegals, or legal operations staff use without formal approval from the firm's IT, security, or compliance function.

children.name: Bias Testing and Alignment
children.blurb: Bias testing and alignment covers evaluating model outputs for unfair treatment across protected attributes and checking whether model behavior matches organizational or legal expectations.

sections.body: AI security audits and enterprise enablement is the work of making legal AI systems safe and governable before and while lawyers use them. It combines security review, policy design, data handling, and testing for bias. In practice, teams inventory AI tools, map data flows, check vendor claims, and run controlled tests on model outputs. They also write rules for acceptable use and monitor for tools that appear without approval. This field treats legal AI as an enterprise system with legal, ethical, and confidentiality risks, not just a drafting shortcut.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are relatively mature. Data loss prevention and access control have established methods from general IT security, and threat modelling can borrow from software security practice. Bias testing remains hard because legal bias is context dependent and often lacks clean labels. Shadow AI is a moving target as staff adopt new tools faster than policy can keep up. The legal stakes are real: this site tracks 146 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which shows courts are still shaping the rules. Audits can document controls and surface gaps, but they cannot guarantee a model will not leak data, produce biased advice, or create new liability.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The AI Enablement Audit is the starting point, giving a structured way to review tools, owners, data, and controls across a legal team. Threat Modelling for Legal AI goes deeper into adversarial risks, misuse cases, and failure modes specific to legal work. Data Loss Prevention and Sanitisation covers the technical and procedural controls for keeping confidential material out of unauthorised models and outputs. Shadow AI in Legal Teams addresses the human and organisational side, including detection, policy, and safe alternatives for unsanctioned use. Bias Testing and Alignment closes the set by examining how to test outputs for unfair or misaligned behaviour and what alignment work can and cannot fix. A reader would move from the audit page to threat modelling for risk design, then to data loss prevention and shadow AI for operational controls, and finally to bias testing for model behaviour.
